title: Vision Transformers and Multimodal Meaning · Level 1
slo: Explain how image and text information can be connected in a multimodal model.

exercises.question_text: What do vision transformers create to represent visual features and their relationships?

options.rationale: Visual embeddings are vectors representing image features. They also capture contextual relationships among those features.
Language tokens are units used to process text. They do not represent visual relationships in an image.
options.better_fit: Language tokens are appropriate when a model processes written words.

feedback.intrinsic: This would process text rather than image content.
feedback.instructional: Visual embeddings represent features in image patches.

options.rationale: An image label names a predicted category. It does not encode rich relationships among visual features.
options.better_fit: Image labels are appropriate for basic image-classification outputs.

feedback.intrinsic: This would return a category instead of a feature representation.

options.rationale: Bounding boxes locate regions containing objects. They do not encode contextual visual features.
options.better_fit: Bounding boxes are appropriate when locating objects in an image.

feedback.intrinsic: This would mark locations without representing image features.
feedback.instructional: Visual embeddings represent features and their relationships.

exercises.explanation: Visual embeddings represent visual features and their relationships.

exercises.question_text: Which statements describe cross-model attention and shared vector space? Select all that apply.

options.text: It relates language and vision embeddings
options.rationale: Cross-model attention defines relationships across language and vision embeddings. It connects representations from the two modalities.
A shared vector space is a unified representation. It provides a common place for related language and visual embeddings.

options.text: It labels every pixel by object
options.rationale: Labeling every pixel is semantic segmentation. It does not by itself connect language embeddings with vision embeddings.
options.better_fit: Pixel labels are appropriate for semantic segmentation tasks.

feedback.intrinsic: This would identify object areas without connecting them to language.
feedback.instructional: Cross-model attention relates language and vision embeddings.

options.rationale: Finding rectangular regions is object detection. It does not define a shared representation for language and vision.
options.better_fit: Rectangular object regions are appropriate outputs for object detection.

feedback.intrinsic: This would locate objects without linking them to words.
feedback.instructional: Shared space relates language and visual embeddings.

exercises.explanation: Cross-model attention connects embeddings in a unified representation.

exercises.question_text: A visual vocabulary is a multidimensional map of related visual features.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This misidentifies the purpose of visual vocabulary.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Visual embeddings form a multidimensional map of related visual features.

exercises.explanation: A visual vocabulary organizes related visual features.

exercises.question_text: Cross-model attention defines relationships only among vision embeddings, not between language and vision embeddings.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This leaves language disconnected from vision.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Cross-model attention defines relationships between the two embedding types.

exercises.explanation: Cross-model attention relates language embeddings with vision embeddings.

exercises.question_text: What can a vision transformer infer when visual features often appear together? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Repeated co-occurrence can show contextual relatedness. The model can learn that the visual patterns are associated.

options.text: Their vectors can be similarly related
options.rationale: Features occurring in similar contexts can receive related representations. This reflects learned visual associations.

options.text: The model understands objects like a person
options.rationale: Learning visual associations does not create human-like understanding. The model relates characteristics rather than comprehending objects as people do.
options.better_fit: Human-like understanding is appropriate when describing a person's interpretation of objects.

feedback.intrinsic: This overstates what recurring patterns establish.
feedback.instructional: Co-occurrence supports contextual relationships, not human understanding.

options.text: The model uses only word meanings
options.rationale: This inference begins with visual characteristics in images. It is not based only on word meanings.
options.better_fit: Word meanings are appropriate when reasoning within a language vocabulary.

feedback.intrinsic: This ignores the visual patterns in the image.

exercises.explanation: Co-occurring visual features can be contextually related.

exercises.question_text: A team receives a previously unseen customer photo and needs the model to produce a written scene description. Which capability should it use?

options.rationale: Image description connects visual features with associated language. It gives semantic interpretation beyond a single category.
Classification predicts a main-subject category. That is the narrower capability named in the question.
options.better_fit: Image classification is appropriate when the goal is to identify a fruit type.

feedback.intrinsic: The result would be only a category name.
feedback.instructional: Image description provides semantic interpretation beyond one label.

options.rationale: Detection identifies locations of objects in an image. It does not itself generate a language description.
options.better_fit: Detecting object regions is appropriate when locating several items in a scene.

feedback.intrinsic: The result could show locations but not describe the scene.
feedback.instructional: Description requires language associated with visual features.

options.rationale: Pixel classification assigns a class to each image area. It does not produce a written interpretation of the scene.
options.better_fit: Classifying image pixels is appropriate for semantic segmentation.

feedback.intrinsic: The result could outline objects without explaining them in words.
feedback.instructional: Semantic interpretation creates an image description.

exercises.explanation: Describing an unfamiliar image goes beyond one label.

exercises.question_text: When hat-like and head-like features occur together, a vision transformer understands hats and heads as humans do.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This claims more than the learned visual pattern supports.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The model relates visual characteristics but does not understand objects as people do.

exercises.explanation: It can infer a visual relationship without human-like understanding.

exercises.question_text: To describe an unfamiliar image, a combined model only needs to assign one image label.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This produces only a limited category name.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Image description goes beyond classification by connecting visual features with language in shared space.

exercises.explanation: A description needs visual features connected with associated language.

exercises.question_text: What can paired images and text descriptions enable? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Paired data aligns image information with descriptive language. This supports combining language and vision encoders.
Descriptions link language representations to image representations. This can connect language and visual vocabularies.
Combined language and vision encoders form a multimodal model. Paired image-text data helps train that combination.
Paired training links language and visual embeddings. It does not eliminate the visual representations needed for images.
options.better_fit: Visual embeddings remain appropriate for representing features extracted from images.

feedback.intrinsic: Removing visual embeddings would remove the image-side representation.
feedback.instructional: Paired training combines and links both embedding types.

exercises.explanation: Paired data links language and vision rather than replacing either.

exercises.question_text: What does a language vocabulary encode?

options.rationale: A language vocabulary contains embeddings for words. Those embeddings encode semantic relationships among words.
Relationships among visual features belong to a visual vocabulary. A language vocabulary instead concerns words.
options.better_fit: A visual vocabulary is appropriate for relating color, shape, contrast, and texture.

feedback.intrinsic: This substitutes image features for words.
feedback.instructional: Language vocabulary represents semantic relationships among words.

options.rationale: Object locations are detection outputs. They are not semantic relationships represented by language embeddings.
options.better_fit: Object locations are appropriate when using bounding boxes for object detection.

feedback.intrinsic: This changes a word-meaning task into a location task.
feedback.instructional: Language vocabulary concerns words, not image regions.

options.rationale: Pixel color channels store image values such as RGB components. They do not encode relationships among words.
options.better_fit: Pixel color channels are appropriate when representing the raw colors of a digital image.

feedback.intrinsic: This focuses on pixels instead of language.
feedback.instructional: Language vocabulary is built from word embeddings.

exercises.explanation: Language vocabulary encodes semantic relationships among words.

exercises.question_text: Images paired with text descriptions can link a language vocabulary with a visual vocabulary.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This would separate the image from its associated language.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Paired images and descriptions allow language and vision encoders to be combined.

exercises.explanation: Paired data can link the two vocabularies.

exercises.question_text: A language vocabulary represents relationships among words, whereas a visual vocabulary represents relationships among visual features.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This would blur the distinction between word and image-feature representations.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Language vocabulary encodes word relationships; visual vocabulary encodes visual-feature relationships.

exercises.explanation: The two vocabularies represent different modalities.

flashcards.back: A multidimensional map of related visual features.

flashcards.front: Does visual context equal human understanding?
flashcards.back: No. The model relates visual characteristics without human understanding.
It relates language embeddings to vision embeddings.
It combines language and vision encoders into a multimodal model.
